newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares start lower on Telekom debut.
newsitem.headline: German shares start lower on Telekom debut.

text.p: German shares started bourse trade lower on Monday on the market debut of Deutsche Telekom, the newly-floated former state telecommunications giant.
Traders said trade in Telekom, Europe's largest-ever equity issue, would dominate the day's trade and widely expected its shares to gain significantly on its issue price of 28.50 marks a share.
"There's only one subject to today and that's Telekom. Don't go looking for much action elsewhere in the market," said one Frankfurt trader.
The DAX 30 index of leading German shares traded 15.55 points lower at 2,780.25 in late morning trade, with overall turnover described as weak.
Traders said they expected the market to consolidate further below the 2,800 level, which had been breached for the first time in electronic trade on Friday.
Telekom shares were quoted above their issue price in "grey trade", the market carried on by brokers among themselves and not subject to official controls.
Frankfurt-based broker Schnigge & Partner said shares in grey market dealings were quoted around 31.50 and 32.50 marks at 1000 GMT, compared to a level of around 33 marks earlier in the day.
Brokerage group Instinet said it saw prices of around 31,60 marks to 31.45 being quoted, adding that volumes were increasing.
"We reckon that this means the share price will swing between 31 and 31.50 marks," said one Instinet broker.
An official estimate of the trading price of Telekom shares is due around 1030 GMT.
One positive impetus on Deutsche Telekom shares was seen as the likelihood of institutional investors, disappointed by their allocation, seeking to buy more shares on the open market.
"Some of the foreign allotments were very disappointing. The UK portion was very, very small," one trader said.
The issue was five times oversubscribed despite a last-minute widening of the amount of shares on offer.
The trader added that the early trading levels of the stock was likely to be erratic with a steadier trend seen on Tuesday.
"Tomorrow, when New York and Tokyo will be in, that's when we'll probably see a clear trend," said the trader.
New York trade is due to start later on Monday with trade on the Japanese market to begin Tuesday.
Among other shares, stocks in retailer Karstadt fell 26 marks to 549 marks after it said on Friday that it expected 1996 earnings to be below the 1995 level.
